title: Energy Pyramid Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Biology
description: Interactive MicroSim that visualizes energy, biomass, and organism-count pyramids with adjustable producer input and efficiency.

learningObjectives: Calculate the energy available at each trophic level by adjusting producer input and transfer efficiency using the 10% rule.
Compare energy, biomass, and organism-count pyramids to explain why food chains are limited in length and why aquatic pyramids can invert.
prerequisites: Understands producers, consumers, and trophic levels
Knows the 10% rule / energy transfer concept

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration with comparative toggles and immediate visual feedback
keyQuestions: How much energy reaches each trophic level when efficiency drops below 10%?
What happens to the pyramid shape when you switch to biomass or numbers?
Why can aquatic numbers pyramids appear inverted?
commonMisconceptions: Energy transfer can exceed 10% between any two levels.
Adding apex predators does not impact lower-level energy requirements.
Biomass and numbers pyramids must always have the same shape as energy pyramids.
assessmentOpportunities: Students justify whether an added apex level is sustainable at a selected efficiency.
Learners compare and contrast energy vs. biomass vs. numbers pyramids in writing.
